exposure: Intestinal microbiota manipulation (antibiotic treatment, E. coli gavage, B. infantis gavage, saline)
outcome: Gene expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL1b, IL6, IL2, TNF-a, toll-like receptors 2-6)
cohort: The study participants were neonatal C57BL/6J mouse pups.
finding: The neonatal gut microbiota significantly modulated the neuroinflammatory response and severity of hypoxic-ischemic brain injury, with E. coli increasing edematous injury volume and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, while B. infantis appeared protective.
followup_time: Postnatal Day 13 (P13), which was 72 hours after the hypoxic-ischemic event.
